title: Tibber Energy dashboard shows large negative consumption around midnight
body: After updating to Home Assistant 2021.12.0 late last night, my Energy dashboard shows large negative consumption around midnight for all my meters. I have no energy production, so this is clearly wrong. It happens on both a Supervised installation and an OS installation. The last working Core version was 2021.11.5, and I cannot see anything useful in the logs.

symptoms_visible: After updating to Home Assistant 2021.12.0, all my Energy dashboard meters show large negative consumption around midnight even though I have no energy production.
N0.label: N0 negative midnight consumption reported

symptoms_visible: The Tibber accumulated-consumption sensor rises during the day, but the Energy dashboard records a large negative value when that sensor resets around midnight.
The negative value repeats on later nights without another Home Assistant update, and its size is approximately the preceding day's consumption.
N1.label: N1 Tibber reset pattern established

symptoms_visible: After updating to Home Assistant 2021.12.2, the Energy dashboard still records the same large negative Tibber consumption around midnight.
N2_x.label: N2_x ordinary update aftermath

symptoms_visible: Immediately after I patched the Tibber component and restarted Home Assistant, the Energy dashboard showed one unusually large positive consumption peak.
The following hourly values returned to their expected size while I waited for the next midnight rollover.
N3.label: N3 local rollover patch installed

symptoms_visible: With the patched Tibber component, midnight passed without the large negative consumption value.
Apart from the one-time peak when the patch was introduced, the hourly graph looks normal and the completed day's total matches the accumulated-consumption value at midnight.
N4.label: N4 rollover behavior verified

symptoms_visible: After installing and verifying a Home Assistant build containing the Tibber rollover fix, accumulated consumption crosses midnight without adding a large negative value to the Energy dashboard.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Which integration and entity are configured as the Energy dashboard consumption source?
What sensor supplies these meter readings?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm using Tibber data, specifically sensor.accumulated_consumption_xxx, as the Energy dashboard input. Other affected users here are using the same Tibber sensor.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm not using Tibber or a resetting accumulated sensor; this is a continuously increasing physical meter entity from another integration.
I use the same Tibber accumulated-consumption entity but have renamed it locally.

question_patterns: What does the source sensor itself do before and around midnight?
Does the underlying sensor decrease, reset, or continue rising when the negative dashboard value appears?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The accumulated-consumption sensor rises steadily during the day and resets around midnight. My two meters do not reset at exactly the same moment: one appears just before midnight and the other just after it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The source sensor never resets or decreases; it remains a lifetime total while the dashboard alone becomes negative.
The reset occurs a few seconds later on one meter, but both reset close to midnight.

question_patterns: How does the size of the negative value compare with the preceding day's usage?
Is there a consistent relationship between the reset and the negative amount?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The incorrect negative amount is approximately the previous day's total. For example, about 17 kWh of usage is followed by roughly -17 kWh in the first interval of the new day.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The graph color differs between my phone and desktop browser, but the numeric negative amount is the same.

edges.comment: Comments c0-c5 and c1 are folded into one simulated user side. They establish that the affected source is Tibber accumulated_consumption, that its daily reset aligns with the dashboard drop, and that multiple Tibber users see the same behavior.

solution.intent: Treat the issue as already corrected by an ordinary Home Assistant 2021.12 patch update and ask the user to update without confirming that the build contains the Tibber rollover fix.
solution.concrete_example: Update from 2021.12.0 to the current 2021.12 patch release and check the next Energy dashboard rollover.

edges.comment: A second affected user installed 2021.12.2 and observed the same negative value after midnight because the proposed Tibber fix was not included. This user is folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Keep the Tibber accumulated-consumption entities as total sensors, but make their real daily rollover explicit by setting last_reset when the accumulated value decreases around midnight; retain ordinary within-day decreases as corrections rather than meter resets.
solution.concrete_example: Patch the Tibber accumulatedConsumption and accumulatedProduction entities so a decrease associated with the midnight timestamp updates last_reset to that local midnight. Do not classify every small hourly decrease as a reset.
solution.inference_hint: The users supplied the reset timing, sensor values, and negative dashboard deltas. The conclusion that STATE_CLASS_TOTAL needs a last_reset boundary—and that TOTAL_INCREASING remains inaccurate because Tibber performs legitimate hourly downward corrections—is engineer-side interpretation.

edges.comment: The reporter manually applied the candidate Tibber sensor patch and restarted Home Assistant. That persistent local modification creates a new system state. The immediate one-time positive peak is recorded as an observable aftermath, not as a verdict on the patch.

question_patterns: Please leave the patched installation running through the next midnight and tell me what the Energy dashboard records.
After the next daily rollover, do you see another large negative value?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Midnight passed without incident. I did not get the large negative value. There was the one bump when I first introduced the patch, but after that the graph looks good.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patched installation still produced the same negative value when the sensor reset at midnight.
Midnight passed without a negative spike, but the reset occurred several seconds after 00:00.

edges.comment: Pre-landing verification of the candidate local patch is a measurement. A second tester independently reported no midnight spike and later confirmed that the completed Energy dashboard total matched the accumulated-consumption value at midnight; both users are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Ship the verified Tibber rollover handling so accumulated-consumption sensors declare their actual daily reset through last_reset while preserving ordinary hourly corrections, then ask the user to verify a build containing that fix before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Use a Home Assistant build containing the verified Tibber accumulated-consumption rollover handling, keep the existing accumulated_consumption entity selected in Energy, and retest through midnight to confirm that no negative daily-total-sized delta is added.

edges.comment: The candidate behavior was verified across midnight before the fix was treated as accepted. The terminal state represents subsequent user verification on a Home Assistant build containing that same rollover handling, not release scheduling.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: Tibber accumulated-consumption is a daily-resetting total that can also receive smaller within-day corrections; after its state class changed to total without a usable last_reset boundary, the midnight reset was accumulated as a large negative delta.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the dashboard drop coincides with the Tibber sensor reset, approximately equals the previous day's total, repeats without another update, and disappears when the candidate rollover handling is tested across midnight.
The fix must preserve the Tibber accumulated-consumption entity for Energy, use last_reset to mark the genuine daily rollover, and avoid treating ordinary hourly corrections as new meter cycles.
Must not claim that an ordinary 2021.12 patch update resolves the issue unless the installed build is known to contain the Tibber rollover fix; that move was falsified in the thread.
Must ask the user to verify a Home Assistant build containing the fix through a midnight rollover before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Home Assistant user who can compare entity histories, reason about hourly energy pricing, edit integration source files, restart Core, inspect SQLite statistics, and test a candidate patch.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, analytical, and cooperative. Supplies graphs and timing observations, distinguishes hypotheses from observations, warns others about database-editing pitfalls, and reports test results promptly.
